title: Test annotation qualifier composition without losing value checks or metadata
applies_when: A Python runtime checker or schema introspector handles TypedDict Required, NotRequired, ReadOnly and Annotated through an origin/argument dispatch loop; individual wrappers work but supported nesting may fall into an unknown-type path.
lesson: Test documented wrapper compositions, not just each wrapper independently. PEP 655 permits Annotated outside or inside Required/NotRequired. Compare both orders using a valid value, wrong value and missing key; absence is not a nullable value. Include total/non-total dictionaries and concrete/string annotations with the supported typing provider. If normalization must cross Annotated to find a qualifier, retain its metadata for actual custom-checker callbacks in inner-before-outer order, including duplicates; stripping all metadata can repair the built-in check while breaking extensions. In the cited Typeguard revision, outer Annotated hides the qualifier from check_typed_dict; the later dispatch unwraps only Annotated and silently leaves the underlying value unchecked. A metadata callback is a necessary control for the proposed normalization, not a performance test.
avoid_when: This is not permission to strip arbitrary wrappers or reorder custom constraints. Required and NotRequired together are an invalid contract, not another supported permutation. ReadOnly concerns mutation typing; checking its value type does not enforce runtime immutability. Provider/interpreter features differ, and static typing alone does not promise every library's runtime API. Type aliases, forward-reference scopes, inherited or generic dictionaries need their own qualification. The cited repair is locally tested but not merged or official CI; this is not evidence that knowledge retrieval improves discovery or PR conversion.

evidence.note: Defines both Annotated nesting orders with Required/NotRequired as valid; its specification separately rejects combining Required and NotRequired. This establishes a contract to test, not that every runtime checker implements it.
Annotated preserves metadata order, flattens nested metadata from the innermost annotation and does not remove duplicates. Unknown metadata does not erase the underlying type.

Pinned qualifier loop handles Required/NotRequired/ReadOnly but stops at Annotated. Inspect the subsequent check_type_internal dispatch as well; the source mechanism is not a complete package or platform verdict.

Public candidate regression/control matrix includes both nesting orders, requiredness, string annotations and real checker-lookup metadata callbacks. Candidate source is not upstream acceptance; native run logs remain separate.

Submitted Ready bugfix reports native original/fixed comparisons, metadata controls and the unchanged baseline mypy failure. Publication is not merge, full CI acceptance or evidence of learned-selector efficacy.
